Items.Authors: Vladimir Shmagin, Mikhail Sachkov, Sergey Sichevsky, Evgeniy A. Kopylov
Items.Title: The field camera unit imaging instrument onboard Spektr-UF space mission
Items.Abstract: Spektr-UF (Spektrum-UV, WSO-UV) is a third mission of the SPEKTR series of the Russian Space Program for the deep space exploration. The observatory includes a 170 cm aperture telescope, Spectrographs and Imagers. We provide an updated information on the project periodically. Here we present an updated information on the Field Camera Unit instrument. One of the important changes in the mission is that Russia (ROSCOSMOS) has taken over the responsibility to build all instruments of the mission including detector for Far UV and Near UV spectral ranges.

Items.Authors: Alexandre Boucaud, Pierre Antilogus, Eric Aubourg, Antoine Bernard, Johan Bregeon, Patrick Breugnon, Julien Coridian, Hervé Croizet, Guillaume Daubard, Kevin Fanning, Fabrice Gallo, Anthony S. Johnson, Claire Juramy-Gilles, Pierre Karst, Mile Kusulja, Eric Lagorio, Travis Lange, Didier Laporte, Juan-Carlos Lazarte, Margaux Lopez, Aurelien Marini, Stuart Marshall, Dmitry Onoprienko, Hannah M. M. Pollek, Max Turri, Yousuke Utsumi, Pierre Verdier, Francis Vezzu, Françoise Virieux, Téo Weicherding
Items.Title: The filter exchange system of the LSSTCam at the Vera C. Rubin Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Filter Exchange System of the LSSTCam at the Vera C. Rubin Observatory  is a critical subsystem enabling the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) by  performing rapid, repeatable exchanges among five large-format filters within a  highly constrained in-camera volume. Since the start of on-sky operations in  April 2025, the FES has routinely performed up to 40 filter exchanges per night,  completing each change in under 90 seconds with a positioning  repeatability of 100 micrometres in the focal plane.   Safety and reliability are ensured through a dedicated software architecture.  Drawing on over a year of operational experience, we report on  the in-situ performance of this sophisticated system within the observatory environment,  characterize the key performance metrics, and discuss how specific design  choices have influenced system behaviour and reliability in practice.

Items.Authors: Shubhangi Jain, Judhajeet Basu, Mahesh Babu, Bharat Chandra, Rekesh Mohan, Margarita Safonova, Jayant Murthy, Praveen Kumar, Shubham Ghatul
Items.Title: The FUV Imaging Satellite (FISAT): a 4U far-UV imaging telescope
Items.Abstract: Despite the scientific importance of far-ultraviolet (FUV) observations, few dedicated FUV imaging missions are planned in the near future. We present the Far-Ultraviolet Imaging Satellite (FISAT), a compact 80 mm Ritchey–Chrétien telescope operating in the 130–180 nm band with a 3° field of view, capable of detecting sources as faint as 19 AB (1200 s, SNR = 5). Designed for CubeSat platforms, FISAT will conduct a 6–12 month survey focused on daily monitoring of transient phenomena. A key objective is the systematic observation of novae in M31, enabling high-cadence FUV light curves that probe nova evolution, UV flashes, and progenitor properties. Complemented by optical data, FISAT will enhance nova detection rates and improve constraints on nova populations. The mission may also capture other energetic transients, including supernovae and FBOTs, and will include a Galactic plane survey. Its small form factor and simple design significantly reduce development time and cost. FISAT will

Items.Authors: Walter M. Harris, Jason Corliss, Dolon Bhattacharyya, Edwin Mierkiewicz, Gonzalo Cucho Padin
Items.Title: The Hydrogen Emission Line Interferometric eXplorer (HELIX): suborbital exploration of exospheric hydrogen at high spectral resolving power
Items.Abstract: The Hydrogen Emission Line Interferometric eXplorer (HELIX) is a sounding rocket experiment to study the lineshape of hydrogen Ly-a emission in the terrestrial geocorona. The science instrument is an all-reflective spatial heterodyne spectrometer (RSHS), a self-scanning two-beam Fourier Transform Spectrometer (FTS) that combines high spectral resolving power and high etendue in a compact format. The HELIX RSHS provides a resolving power of R~250000 (e.g., dV = 1.2 km/s, T > 50 K) that is sufficient to observe coronal hydrogen in an optically thin column over a square aperture covering 0.29 x 0.29 deg. HELIX would launch in early 2028 at 12:00-14:00 Solar Time to an estimated peak altitude > 310 km for ~430 s of data acquisition. It would obtain observations of the intensity and lineshape of geocoronal hydrogen at zenith angles of ~50 and ~100 degrees. In this presentation we review the scientific and technical drivers for the HELIX instrument and mission design.

Items.Authors: Feifan Zhang, Banglong Peng, Baolong Chen, Zengxiang Zhou, Jianping Wang
Items.Title: The influence of eccentric arm shape on collision possibilities of theta-phi positioners based on the Monte-Carlo method
Items.Abstract: Fiber positioners are the key instruments in many modern multi-object spectroscopic telescopes. To guarantee no blind area, they are densely packed with shared working space, leading to possible collisions between eccentric arms of positioners. Collision possibilities and collision avoidance algorithms have been widely studied. However, the influence of eccentric arm shape on collision possibilities have not been studied. In this study, we explore the collision possibilities of theta-phi positioners with different eccentric arm shapes. We establish the kinematic models based on the D-H method. The collisions are detected according to equations derived from geometry. Based on the abovementioned methods, for each shape, simulations based on the Monte Carlo method are carried out to obtain the collision possibility. According to the results, the shape with least collision possibility will be chosen. This study can provide a reference for the design of theta-phi positioners.

Items.Authors: Gabriel Giono, Harald Ottacher, Gunter Laky, Jorge Lucio Tonfat Seclen, Karl Hofmann, Robert Wallner, Parviz Azhdarzadeh, Johann Hasiba, Iñigo Bouzas, Iñigo Poncela, Marco Truglio, Santiago Serrano, Søren K. Christensen, Asger B. Hebsgaard, Jacob S. Jørvang, Torbjørn Østmoe, Petter Øya, Andreas F. Haavik, Åsmund Braathen, Frank Eckardt, Amir Hasanbegovic, Ola Ro, Sebastian Benoit, Roland Ottensamer, Gerald Mösenlechner, Armin Luntzer, Dominik Loidolt, Roman Zoufal, Antonio Rodriguez-Senin, Carlos Corral van Damme, Thibaut Prod' Homme, Timo Ruehl, Marco Sirianni, Luc Boucher, Jens Loehring, Jean-Philippe Halain
Items.Title: The instrument control unit for the Arrakihs mission
Items.Abstract: The Arrakihs Electronics Box (EBOX), instrument control subsystem for the Arrakihs instrument is presented in this contribution. The EBOX includes redundant Power Supply Units, redundant high-performance quad-core Data Processing Units, redundant milliKelvins stability Thermal Control Units, two Near-Infrared Interfaces to the NIR detector chain processing guide stars windows and full frame pre-processing for non-destructive read-out scheme and a multi-core application software handling the fine-guidance system, multi-accumulation computation and real-time compression.

Items.Authors: António Amorim, Mercedes Filho, Remko Stuik, Dirk Lesman, Sander Kwast, Paulo Garcia, João Canais
Items.Title: The integration and acceptance of the elevation platform for the WSS subsystem of the METIS/ELT
Items.Abstract: The ELP is the main support structure for the WSS subsystem of the METIS first light instrument for the ELT.  All ELP components have been manufactured and, in May 2025, the ELP was fully assembled at the manufacturer, partly reproducing the assembly procedure of the ELP on the Nasmyth platform in Chile. After a visit from the METIS Consortium and ESO personnel to inspect the assembled ELP, the ELP Acceptance was planned, which would include training of Chile ESO personnel to assemble the ELP and preliminary alignment measurements of the ELP.  In this talk we will describe the challenges in the manufacture and assembly of the ELP, as well as the results from alignment measurements and the Acceptance.

Items.Authors: Masato Kagitani, Fuminori Tsuchiya, Go Murakami, Atsushi Yamazaki, Kameda Shingo, Kazuo Yoshioka, Ryoichi Koga, Umi Enokidani, Riko Shimizu, Masaki Kuwabara, Yuki Oue
Items.Title: The LAPYUTA mission: overview of mid-dispersion UV spectrograph and development updates
Items.Abstract: The LAPYUTA mission is a candidate ultraviolet space telescope for JAXA's 6th M-class program. Its mid-resolution ultraviolet spectrograph (MRS) covers 110--190 nm with a spectral resolution of 0.02 nm and a central-field spatial resolution of 0.10 arcsec FWHM. The MRS employs a simple high-throughput optical design using a toroidal holographic grating. We present the spatial-resolution error budget, optical layout, and grating tolerance analysis. The error budget corresponds to a Gaussian-equivalent RMS width of 0.043 arcsec. The tolerance analysis shows that the spectrograph-induced image degradation can remain within the allocated budget by compensating focus and grating angles. We also describe post-processing image deblurring using simultaneous zeroth-order imaging to correct spacecraft attitude disturbances. Simulations of centroiding and phase-only correlation methods indicate that suitable displacement measurements are feasible.

Items.Authors: Sonja O. T. Choi, Warren Foster, Andrew Monson, Chad Bender, Roger Angel, Zsombor Antal, Joel Berkson, Nina Brown, Gilberto Chavez-Lopez, Megan Delamer, Trevor Dugan, Kevin Gilliam, Peter Gray, Yiyang Huang, Chris Kruep, Riley Mikkelsen, Fernando Parra, Jason Patrou, Milan Riha, Brian Scaramella, Christian Schwab, Melanie Sisco, William Thompson, Richard Wortley, Dennis Zaritsky, David Zeller
Items.Title: The Large Fiber Array Spectroscopic Telescope: optical system throughput analysis
Items.Abstract: The Large Fiber Array Spectroscopic Telescope (LFAST) is an array of small, low-cost fiber telescopes for high-resolution spectroscopy. We present the throughput budget of our first prototype unit across 400–1700 nm, in which we examine the optical train from the 0.76 m, f/3.3 primary mirror to the prime-focus corrector, 16 m fiber feed, fiber combiner and spectrograph optics. We also incorporate atmospheric absorption, seeing, coating transmission, and coupling losses in our calculation. The throughput analysis identifies the dominant throughput-limiting components and guides fabrication requirements as well as design improvements that maximize performance gains. It also supports the development of a realistic exposure-time calculator for on-sky testing, enabling science case planning and efficient queue scheduling for LFAST’s operations. Finally, the analysis provides a benchmark for unit-telescope testing and constrains expectations for future expansion to a larger aperture.

Items.Authors: Thomas M. Herbst, Guillermo Blanc, Niv Drory, Oleg Egorov, Kathryn Kreckel, Eduardo Mendez Delgado, Sebastian F. Sanchez, Peter Bizenberger, Evelyn Johnston, José Sánchez-Gallego, Stefanie Wachter
Items.Title: The LVM2 north telescope and instrument
Items.Abstract: The Local Group Explorer (LGE), one of four Explorers that form the After Sloan Digital Sky Survey-V (AS5) program, is a project to spectroscopically map the Milky Way, Local Group galaxies, and the low-surface brightness Universe in both hemispheres. The southern component of LGE will exploit the existing SDSS-V Local Volume Mapper infrastructure at Las Campanas Observatory, while the northern counterpart will require new hardware development at an existing 2-m class telescope. This hardware includes an optical relay for focal ratio matching, an atmospheric dispersion compensator, and a focal plane assembly to host the Integral Field Unit and acquisition/guiding cameras. A large fiber bundle will convey the light from the telescope focus to three, 3-channel spectrographs in an environmentally-controlled chamber. In this paper, we describe the design of the entire LGE facility, from telescope selection to opto-mechanics and infrastructure.

Items.Authors: Francisco Prada, Robert Content, David Jones, Ryan Cooke, Guillermo González de Riverad, Manuel Vázquez, Enrique Pérez, Ariel Goobar, Jens Hjorth, M. Angeles Pérez-García, Luca Izzo, Matthew Hayes, Manuela Abril, Kilian Henríquez, Hector de Paz, Alejandro Leal, Himar Viera, Gabriel Gómez, Daniel Reverte, Sergio Fernández-Acosta, Antonio L. Cabrera-Lavers, Luis A. Rodríguez, Romano Corradi
Items.Title: The MAAT IFU at the GTC: from manufacturing challenge to first light
Items.Abstract: The MAAT Integral Field Unit (IFU) is being developed for the Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC) to enable advanced focal-plane reformatting for spectroscopy. Manufactured by Bertin Winlight, the IFU incorporates a precision image slicer composed of 23 thin mirrors that rearrange the telescope focal plane into a pseudo-slit geometry. During final integration and verification, a critical manufacturing error was identified: all slicer mirrors were produced with their centers of curvature reversed relative to the optical design. This systematic inversion caused beam deviations beyond tolerances, rendering the IFU non-functional. This contribution summarizes the failure and the innovative solution devised by our MAAT optical scientist Robert Content, who redesigned the slicer configuration to enable successful AIV completion in four months. Lessons learned and the path to a compliant IFU are presented, together with first-light results.

Items.Authors: Derek van Winden, Joost van den Born, Ioannis Politopoulos, Julian van den Noort, Jean-Paul Nuismer, Gert Musters, Niels Tromp, Jan Rinze Peterzon, Peter Kunst, Rick Romp, Annemieke Janssen, Menno de Haan, Eddy Elswijk, Elfi Dijkstra, Ramón Navarro, Ester Aranzana
Items.Title: The MICADO first light imager for the ELT: finding the right match: selecting materials for mating surfaces by lifetime testing of MICADO CWM and ADC mechanisms
Items.Abstract: The large size and stringent positioning requirements of first-generation ELT instruments pose significant challenges for designing mechanisms that maintain performance over the instrument’s lifetime. For the development of the Multi-Adaptive Optics Imaging Camera for Deep Observations (MICADO) instrument, cryogenic tests simulating a 10-year lifetime were conducted for the Central Wheel Mechanism (CWM) and Atmospheric Dispersion Corrector (ADC). These tests aimed to investigate wear mechanisms and identify suitable materials for the mechanisms’ mating surfaces. Friction, autocollimator, and image data were used to evaluate bearing–wheel, pinion–wheel, and rotor–roller interfaces made from various materials. Vespel® SP3 and bronze were tested for CWM pinions. Bearings and rollers of gold-coated stainless steel showed the best performance. Nituff®-coated Al6061 showed minimal wear for the wheels. These findings provide guidance for selecting durable material pairings for ELT mechanisms.

Items.Authors: Benoît Sassolas, Laurent Pinard, Christophe Michel, Julien Teillon, Mathieu Cohen, Eric Gendron, Fanny Chemla, Yann Clénet, Ric Davies
Items.Title: The MICADO first light imager for the ELT: manufacturing of the large dichroic plate of its SCAO module
Items.Abstract: MICADO, a first-light instrument on the European Extremely Large Telescope, operates in the NIR, offering imaging, astrometry, spectroscopy, and high-contrast capabilities. The optical design of its single conjugate adaptive optics (SCAO) module features a 305 mm CaF₂ dichroic plate that splits light between AO and the scientific camera, achieving over 97% transmission from 960–2450 nm and >92% reflectivity from 589–960 nm. The front surface has a thin-film optical filter optimized to minimize coating-induced stress and sensitivity to manufacturing errors. Deposition was performed via ion-beam sputtering with careful control of thermal gradients and post-deposition annealing to release internal stress. The back side has a 16-layer broadband anti-reflective coating ensuring >98.5% transmission. Post-coating characterization confirmed uniform transmission over a 290 mm aperture and reflected wavefront errors within specifications, demonstrating high optical performance.

Items.Authors: Federico Biondi, Kateryna Kravchenko, Lenard Spallek, Florian Lang, Andreas Emslander, Fabio Waldhör, Frank Haussmann, Mathias Honsberg, Luis Neumeier, Nancy Ageorges, Dirk Kampf, Matthias Deysenroth, Marika Einsel, Anna Monna, Annemieke Janssen, Julian van den Noort, Elfi Dijkstra, Rick Romp, Derek van Winden, Ester Aranzana, Aysun Soenmez, Naidu Bezawada, Marcus Haug, Barbara Klein, Sriprasanna Annadevara, Jörg Schlichter, Jonas Graf, Hakan Oezdemir, Andreas Pflueger, Julian Ziegleder, Marius Klepper, Sebastian Rabien, Eckhard Sturm, Richard Davies
Items.Title: The MICADO first light imager for the ELT: overview and results of phase I of the Cold system AIT
Items.Abstract: MICADO is the cryogenic near-infrared Multi-AO Imaging Camera and Spectrometer developed for the first-light operations at the ELT, currently in its MAIT phase. Designed to operate in the NIR wavelength range, MICADO features a LN2 continuous flow cryostat that cools the optics, the mechanisms (focal plane wheel, filter wheel, ADC, operational-mode selector, and detector positioning system), and the nine detectors to the operational temperature of 82 K.   The “COLD-AIT” encompasses all activities related to the integration of the cryogenic subsystems into the cryo-vessel and is developed in three stages, following the readiness of subsystems. In this paper, we describe the first phase of the COLD-AIT, which includes the alignment of the cryostat benches, the installation of dummy masses for each subsystem, metrology checks of structural shrinkage during cooldown, and the assessment of the thermal requirements.

Items.Authors: Marcus Haug, Naidu Bezawada, Barbara Klein, Martin Brinkmann, Eric Müller, Mirko Todorovic
Items.Title: The MICADO first light imager for the ELT: thermal-mechanical design of the focal plane detector array
Items.Abstract: The instrument MICADO, the Multi-AO-Imaging-Camera and Spectrometer for Deep Observations, is one of the first light instruments for the future Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). The MICADO focal plane consists of nine HAWAII-4RG-15 near infrared detectors (2.5um cutoff) mounted in a 3x3 ultra-stable mosaic array configuration on an Invar plate. The highly demanding requirement of 10um (p-v) on the surface flatness of the Invar plate was achieved and verified in house. The corresponding pre-amps are hosted together with the detectors but thermally decoupled to minimize any thermal effects to the detectors and their position. The focal plane is thermally stabilized by two redundant control loops for an optimal detector operating temperature range. In this paper we describe the thermal and mechanical design aspects of the focal plane plate, the detector unit and present the first cryogenic test results.

Items.Authors: Anna Monna, Florian Lang, Birgitta Müller, Jörg Schlichter, Sriprasanna Srivalli Annadevara, Lenard Spallek, Frank U. Grupp, Hans-Joachim Hess, Helmut Kravcar, Hanna Kellermann, Ralf Bender
Items.Title: The MICADO first-light imager for the ELT: cryogenic and ambient performances of the MICADO main selection mechanism
Items.Abstract: The Main Selection Mechanism (MSM) is the cryogenic mechanism that will allow to switch between the 4 operational modes of MICADO, the first light instrument for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). Located inside the MICADO cryostat, the mechanism consists of a main support structure and a rotating platform, where the MICADO Low Resolution Imager, Spectrometer and Pupil Imager modules are located. Manufacturing and procurement for the MSM components was completed in 2025. A first integration of the MSM was performed as a "laboratory setup" for first verification of its functionality and performances. In this paper we present the results of testing the MSM performances and functionality at ambient conditions. In addition, we present the results of cryogenic functionality test of the final integrated and aligned cryogenic mechanism, performed before hand-over of the MSM to the MICADO Project lead Institute, MPE, for its integration inside the instrument cryostat.

Items.Authors: Kenji Emerson, Adwin Boogert, Mike Connelley, John T. Rayner, Charles Lockhart
Items.Title: The observation simulator for the NASA/IRTF spectre spectrograph
Items.Abstract: We present an observation simulator for the SPECTRE spectrograph. SPECTRE is an upcoming, low resolution, broad bandwidth (0.4-4.2 μm), 7.2” field-of-view, three channel, Integral Field Unit (IFU) spectrograph for the NASA Infrared Telescope Facility (IRTF). It is designed for characterizing near-Earth asteroids and spectroscopic follow-up on astrophysical transients. A facility-ready data reduction pipeline is integral to its use by astronomers. We comprehensively simulate observations, accounting for transmissive, emissive, and dispersive effects from the atmosphere, telescope, instrument optics, prisms, and the detector. Instrument calibrations, flat-fielding lamps and spectral arc lamps, can also be simulated. We use our simulations for the on-going development of the SPECTRE data reduction suite, and it can also be used as an exposure time calculator for astronomers to optimize their observing session.

Items.Authors: Bridget C. O'Meara, Randall L. McEntaffer, Alexandra N. Higley, James H. Tutt, Jeffrey De Lucca, Aditi Gangadharan, Nathaniel Hamme, Vadim Burwitz, Gisela Hartner, Andreas Langmeier, Thomas Müller, Surangkhana Rukdee, Thomas Schmidt, Stefano Basso, Alberto Moretti, Daniele Spiga, Max Collon, David Girou, Nicolas Barrière
Items.Title: The opto-mechanical design and alignment of x-ray grating modules for the off-plane grating rocket experiment pathfinder (OGRE-P) mission
Items.Abstract: The Off-plane Grating Rocket Experiment pathfinder (OGRE-P) payload is a sub-orbital sounding rocket payload designed to obtain high-resolution observations. This pathfinder mission will pave the way for subsequent missions to achieve even higher resolution soft X-ray spectra of Capella. The OGRE-P spectrometer will focus incoming light using the Joint European X-ray Telescope (JET-X). An array of six stacks of X-ray reflection gratings will diffract the light, and the resulting soft X-ray spectra will be captured using three focal plane detectors. This paper will focus on the opto-mechanical design for mounting OGRE-P's X-ray grating modules. The mechanical design for mounting and securing the modules to the payload will be discussed. The procedure for aligning the grating stacks to the JET-X optic to meet the required tolerances will also be discussed.

Items.Authors: Simone Garrappa, Yahel Sofer Rimalt, Eran O. Ofek, Sagi Ben-Ami, David Polishook, Alex Bichkovsky, Enrico Segre
Items.Title: The Pan-chromatic Array for Survey Telescopes (PAST) at the Weizmann Astrophysical Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Pan-chromatic Array for Survey Telescopes (PAST) is a modular, cost-effective multi-band imaging facility optimized for rapid photometric follow-up of time-domain surveys such as the Large Array Survey Telescope (LAST) and the ULTRASAT mission. Each unit combines four 14-inch Schmidt-Cassegrain telescopes with dichroic beam splitters to deliver eight simultaneous optical bands spanning 4000–8000 Å. In this contribution, we present the PAST design and highlight key science drivers. We also briefly discuss initial performance and first demonstration observations.

Items.Authors: Liu Chao, Xiaoxia Qiu, Yonghui Hou, Teng Xu, Wei Wei, Yue Sun, Fanghua Jiang, Xuhao Wu, Yuyao Liu
Items.Title: The robust servo linear quadratic regulator tracking control based on the fuzzy linear extended state observer
Items.Abstract: Aiming at the problems of uncertain disturbance effects, dynamic response lag, and poor overall performance in optoelectronic tracking systems, a novel RSLQR tracking control method based on a fuzzy LESO is proposed. In terms of the optimization of the observer, incorporating the model information of the controlled object into the design of the LESO effectively reduces the computational load of the observer. Meanwhile, a fuzzy algorithm is introduced to dynamically adjust the bandwidth of the observer according to the real-time error of the system, enabling accurate estimation of complex and variable disturbances, and significantly enhancing the online adaptive ability of the observer. In terms of the controller design, on the one hand, the correlation quantity from the system tracking error to the state feedback is introduced into the RSLQR control output, enhancing the system's sensitivity to target changes and optimizing the dynamic characteristics of the system.

Items.Authors: Emily Hu, Suresh Sivanandam, Albert Lau, Coby Silayan, Mark Barnet, Shaojie Chen, Gavin Hay, Aaron Tohuvavohu, Norbert Werner, Marianna Dafčíková, Filip Munz, Patrick Nkwari, Jakub Řípa, Andras Pal
Items.Title: The second little ultraviolet camera (LUVCam2)
Items.Abstract: The second Little UltraViolet Camera (LUVCam2) is a 80mm-diameter dual UV-optical space telescope that will observe the UV flares around low-mass stars, with planned flight as a 1U payload aboard the 3U CubeSat BRNoSat in late 2027. LUVCam2 is the second technology demonstration for the LUVCam electronics board, with the first LUVCam (LUVCam1) still operating in low-Earth orbit (launched July 2024). The main upgrade of LUVCam2 is the use of the backside-illuminated GSENSE4040BSI CMOS sensor, promising significant improvement to UV quantum efficiency over the frontside-illuminated model used in LUVCam1. We present the concept of operations, full system architecture, optomechanical, and electrical design for LUVCam2.

Items.Authors: Yuki Moritani, James E. Gunn, Robert H. Lupton, Kiyoto Yabe, Arnaud Le Fur, Craig P. Loomis, Kjetil Dohlen, Ayumi Takahashi, Matthew Wung, Ligia S. de Oliveira, Antonio C. de Oliveira, Graham J. Murray, Shintaro Koshida, Masayuki Tanaka, Naoyuki Tamura
Items.Title: The short-term fiber throughput variation and its suppression detected for Subaru Prime Focus spectrograph/ʻŌnohiʻula
Items.Abstract: PFS (Prime Focus Spectrograph)/ʻŌnohiʻula is a new major instrument at Subaru Telescope, which was developed by the international collaboration. The instrument features wide-field (1.25 deg^2), high-multiplex (~2400) and wide wavelength coverage (380nm-1260nm). The engineering observations identified a critical issue: the relative throughput among the fibers varied by a few % in timescale of a few hours. The variation was caused by tiny change in the air gap at fiber connectors due to the temperature change, and was suppressed by applying the index matching gel.

Items.Authors: Tarathon Intaros, Krittapas Chanchaiworawit, Picha Ruenarrom, Samattachai Tanun, Samaporn Tinyanont, Thansita Thomrungpiyathan, Teerawat Kuha, Auychai Laoyang, Manlika Pinkaew, Apichat Leckngam
Items.Title: The single point diamond turning capability for the next generation astronomical instruments in Thailand
Items.Abstract: The National Astronomical Research Institute of Thailand (NARIT) has established the SEAL Lab to fabricate ultra-precision optical and mechanical components for next-generation astronomical instruments. The lab produces ultra-smooth aluminum mirrors and complex opto-mechanical parts with sub-micrometer accuracy and nanometer-level surface roughness. Early successes include components for DARTS, the TSC-1 satellite, and a cube-sat telescope. By machining complex geometries directly into aluminum, the lab reduces the need for multi-material designs, simplifies thermal management, and enhances durability. SPDT components integrate efficiently with coating and metrology processes, streamlining prototype-to-payload transitions. SEAL Lab represents a key step in advancing Thailand’s ultra-precision manufacturing capabilities and fostering its role in global astronomy and space exploration.

Items.Authors: Mickaël Lacroix, Jean-Christophe Barrière, Marc Besançon, Sylvain Berson, Nathalie Besson, Alexandre Gallas, Rémi Granelli, Jean-Christophe Guillard, Nicolas Jonquères, Yannick Le Noa, Antoine Petiteau, Yann Reinert, Jean-Antoine Rene, Marek Si Mohammed, Etienne Savalle
Items.Title: The test mass simulator (TMSim), a high precision optomechanical OGSE for LISA
Items.Abstract: The LISA instrument contains a stage called Gravitational Reference Sensor (GRS). It operates like a reference for the interferometer measurements. On the ground for calibration purpose, an optomechanical system is needed to replicate this replicate this reference.  CEA is in charge of developing this opto-mechanical system: the Test Mass Simulator (TMSim). The challenge is to design a very stable system (in term of vibration and thermal stability) on one hand and on another hand to be able to make very precise motions (two rotations in set-and-forget mode and one translation in low dynamic).   The proposed paper presents an overview of the compliant mechanism protype design and the first results of its performance tests.

Items.Authors: Mael Boussange, Jean-Baptiste Daban, Arturo López Ariste, René Dorignac, Pierre Nougué-Cazenave, Alexandre Abeille, Eric Chéreau, Maxime Viau, Nicolas Rago, Cyril Panatier, Thomas Peres, Thomas Lavigne, Philippe Sejournant, Damien Ducos, Pierre Brau-Nogue, Christophe Montheil, Chloe Dubois, Loris Langeois, Mathilde Bodet, Julien Girardeau, Timothée Bruno
Items.Title: The Venus Project: building a fully opening tent-dome at the Pic du Midi Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Venus project consists in building fully opening tent-domes at the Pic du Midi Observatory in southern France. These domes have the advantage of eliminating dome seeing, and the flexible fabric that covers them makes the construction, operation, and maintenance works of these domes easier. The first tent-dome of the Observatory, named Venus-Dauzère, is a prototype and will be operational around mid-2026. It is designed to withstand winds of more than 250 km/h, and its water-repellent fabric prevents snow and frost from accumulating on it. Between 2026 and 2028, we will build two other astronomical tent-domes: one to be used in Antarctica, the other to house the old Jean-Rôsch refractor of Pic du Midi. Over a 10-year horizon, the large 16-meter dome of the Bernard Lyot Telescope at Pic du Midi is the one we plan to replace with a tent-dome, in order to house an array of thirty-six 1-meter telescopes specialized for spectropolarimetry, equivalent to a 6-meter telescope.

Items.Authors: Jake Zimmer, Michael Langmayr, Bradley Price, Takeru Hayashi, Daniel P. Weatherill, Rose Gibson, Roger Smith, Andrey Korolev, Michael Gutierrez, Michael Fitzgerald, Nemanja Jovanovic, Ashley Baker, Rob Bertz, Hector Rodriguez
Items.Title: Thermacopia: a novel high channel count thermal control system for precision astronomy
Items.Abstract: We present a compact, high-precision thermal control system that achieves an unusually high channel count in a modular, reconfigurable architecture. The HISPEC implementation provides 40 heater outputs and 80 temperature-sensor inputs in a low-profile rack-mount enclosure, addressing thermal-control demands that exceed the capabilities of traditional Lakeshore controllers or detector-controller–based solutions. The system architecture utilizes a backplane into which dedicated heater or sensor cards are inserted to tailor functionality while minimizing new hardware development. Heater cards support both low-power linear outputs for fine temperature trimming and high-power switching outputs for rapid warm-up. Sensor cards accommodate RTD and diode with programmable current sources and true 24-bit ADCs. Control and telemetry are provided over TCP/IP with integrated fault-handling. Although developed for HISPEC, this architecture is applicable to many thermally controlled instruments.

Items.Authors: Maxime Rombach, Malak Galal, Jonathan Wei, Stefane Caseiro, Corentin Magnenat, Jean-Paul Kneib
Items.Title: Thermal characterization of a 6-positioner, 6.2-mm-pitch module for stage-5 telescopes
Items.Abstract: Fiber positioner modules are a key development for future Stage-5, highly multiplexed, instruments. Similarly to previous fiber positioners they need to sustain challenging environmental conditions such as a large operating temperature range (–20 °C to +30 °C). This paper presents the thermal tests results of the first 6-positioner module prototype and highlights its encouraging performances consistency.

Items.Authors: Adam D. Wilkinson, Robert Spry, Jake Hutchinson, Roy Preece, John-Paul Walker, Rebecca Holleb, Robert Watkins, Emma Ryan, Liam McSherry, Waqas Mir, Greg King, Cédric Pereira, David Miguel Ventura de Castro Alves, Fraser Clarke, Manuel Abreu, Neil Bowles
Items.Title: Thermal design, analysis, and testing of a cryogenic optical system for characterising the Ariel Space Telescope
Items.Abstract: This paper presents recent progress in the thermal design and verification of the Optical Ground Support Equipment (OGSE) developed to test the integrated Ariel payload in a 35 K cryogenic environment. The OGSE must maintain all optics below 70 K to enable detector dark-current verification, and high vibrational stability must be achieved to ensure sub-arcsecond pointing stability.    The OGSE comprises an illumination module and a periscope module. The illumination module uses a two-stage architecture with an actively cooled radiative shield and a thermally isolated optical bench, both linked to cryocoolers via flexible, high-conductivity copper straps. A thermal breadboard has also been constructed and tested to de-risk the illumination module design. This work presents the thermal architectures of the illumination and periscope modules, and reports results from the thermal breadboarding.

Items.Authors: Jiaming Liang, Yonghe Chen, Chuanxin Wei, Xianyi Zhou, Junfei Li, Yuji Zhu
Items.Title: Thermally driven focus control and on-orbit defocus compensation analysis for the ET Transit Telescope
Items.Abstract: The Transit Telescope serves as the core payload of the Earth 2.0 (ET) mission, whose scientific capability critically depends on imaging quality. During launch and orbital insertion, the telescope experiences vibration, gravity release, and orbital thermal environments. These loads induce defocus and degradation of imaging quality. Therefore, on-orbit defocus compensation is necessary. This study proposes a thermally driven focus control method to achieve active focusing. Through thermal-structural-optical coupled analysis, a calibration model relating temperature, displacement, and defocus is established. It identifies the structural regions most sensitive to focus changes. And micrometer-level focusing capability can be achieved through thermal control. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed thermal focusing approach effectively compensates for defocus induced by launch and on-orbit loads. And it meets the imaging accuracy requirements of the Transit Telescope.

Items.Authors: Emma Rautio-Roe, Alexis Hill, Glen Herriot, Jeffrey Crane, Ross Cheriton, Zoran Ljusic, Thushara Gunaratne, Ralph Webber
Items.Title: Thermally stable system design to enable photonic aperture synthesis
Items.Abstract: Photonic aperture synthesis requires precise phase alignment between signal paths. For the PHASER (PHotonic Aperture Synthesis for Enhanced Resolution) laboratory demonstrator, temperature variations introduce path‑length changes and phase drift. To mitigate these effects, a thermally stable enclosure was developed to house all phase-sensitive components. Each wall of the enclosure uses actively controlled resistive heaters, conductive aluminum, and multilayer insulation to establish a uniform thermal boundary. Additional thermal management strategies reduce internal heat loads and mitigate instability caused by component heat dissipation internal to the enclosure. Experimental validation shows enclosure air stability of 13 mK over a 100-hour test, despite lab temperature variations of 3.4 K peak‑to-valley. The fabricated enclosure provides a stable thermal environment for validating photonic aperture synthesis.

Items.Authors: Yi-xin Liu, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang, Qi Feng
Items.Title: Thermal-mechanical analysis of the CMOS focal plane for Earth 2.0's microlensing telescope
Items.Abstract: This paper presents the design, thermal-mechanical analysis, and optimization of the focal plane assembly (FPA) for Earth 2.0's (ET) Microlensing Telescope. ET observes the Kepler field to detect exoplanets using transit and micro-gravitational lensing methods, both of which require extremely high focal-plane stability. To minimize deformation during launch and in-orbit operation, the FPA is built around a low-expansion silicon-carbide baseplate, which is matched to the SiC-packaged GM-CMOS sensor, complemented by Invar and TC4 structural components.  The FPA’s thermal–mechanical performance is evaluated under launch loads and orbital thermal cycling to verify compliance with mission requirements. Design parameters are then refined through geometric optimization. Through this work, we have also established a mature, efficient, and reusable workflow that integrates design, simulation, and optimization.

Items.Authors: Chang Jin Oh, Andrew E. Lowman, Greg A. Smith, Jamison Noenickx, Sukmock Lee, In-Ung Song, Ben Gallagher, Arthur Mihill, Eric Hansen, Fengchuan Liu
Items.Title: Thirty Meter Telescope secondary mirror metrology: tools for characterizing convex asphere features from 3 meters to 3 microns
Items.Abstract: The Thirty Meter Telescope (TMT) adopts a 3.13m diameter convex aspheric secondary mirror (M2), one of the largest convex mirrors ever designed. Large aspheric, convex mirrors are challenging to measure. Extreme smoothness requirements for the TMT M2 make the metrology and fabrication harder. Specifically, the mirror surface must be precisely measured and evaluated at several spatial scales: 1) the mirror conic and curvature; 2) low order Zernike (Z5-Z15) and low spatial frequency (>143mm period) features; 3) mid spatial frequencies (143-5mm), 4) high spatial frequencies (5-0.08mm), and 5) surface roughness (0.080-0.0025mm).  The University of Arizona team at the Wyant College of Optical Sciences designed the metrology suite for the TMT M2 features sub-aperture Fizeau interferometry with stitching for low and mid spatial frequencies, sub-aperture deflectometry for high spatial frequencies, and microroughness measurements for the smallest features.

Items.Authors: Christina D. Moraitis, Stephen S. Eikenberry, Tyler Thomas, Amanda Townsend, David Smith, Intouch Srijumnong, Aiden Akers, Vincent Miller, Henry Corbett, Megan Dubay
Items.Title: Time-domain spectroscopy with OPASpec at Robinson Observatory
Items.Abstract: We present commissioning results from OPASpec, a dual-channel, fiber-fed optical spectrograph (R ~ 3000) developed for the Original PolyOculus Array (OPA) and first deployed on the 0.5-m telescope at Robinson Observatory in Orlando, Florida. High-cadence spectra of T Coronae Borealis revealed minute-scale variability in H-alpha, H-beta, and He I/He II emission, motivating multiple follow-up observations with HARPS-N and the ARCES echelle at Apache Point Observatory. OPASpec also captured flare spectra from AD Leo, allowing tests of coronal mass ejection (CME) search diagnostics. Although no CMEs were detected, the observations confirmed OPASpec’s suitability for time-domain stellar spectroscopy in search of M-dwarf CMEs. These results establish OPASpec’s readiness for future deployment with the full OPA array at Mount Laguna Observatory.

Items.Authors: Sheng-Feng Lin
Items.Title: Tolerancing of short focal length reflecting mirrors system for remote sensing instruments with sub-meter resolution
Items.Abstract: Compact three-mirror telescope architectures remain particularly challenging due to their intrinsic alignment sensitivity, geometric packaging constraints, and DfMA driven limitations during assembly. The intermediate point located between the primary and secondary mirrors is especially critical, as it influences stray-light control, metrology accessibility, and system-level performance verification throughout AIT. A detailed understanding of the coupling among fabrication errors, alignment-induced deviations, and resulting residual aberrations is therefore essential for predicting system performance and enabling effective iterative correction during integration. This work is performed within the framework of an experimental RSI program targeting sub-0.4-m GSD imaging performance. The paper introduces a tolerancing approach developed to support DfMA-driven optimization of a short-focal-length, three-mirror reflective telescope intended for next-generation sub-meter-class RSIs.

Items.Authors: Ali Ghari Zadeh, Zhemin Cai, Timothy Chin, Jonathan Moller, Helen McGregor, Dylan Simpfendorfer, Yizheng Wang, Jon Lawrence, Jessica Zheng, Chris Coote, Dani Guzman
Items.Title: Topology optimisation of lightweight optical mount for GNAO adaptive optics bench
Items.Abstract: This paper presents a lightweight, high-stability design methodology for aluminium mounts used in the Gemini North Adaptive Optics bench, a key structural subsystem of the next-generation adaptive optics instrument for this telescope. Finite element analysis and topology optimisation are employed to reduce structural mass while maintaining high stiffness and optical alignment accuracy. The proposed workflow is applied to the design of six optical mounts for eight optical elements. The resulting designs provide lightweight, stiff, and vibration-resistant structures with excellent alignment stability. In addition, alignment mechanisms on the mounts retain three degrees of freedom adjustment for the flat mirrors as well as full six DOF adjustment capability for other optics. This light-weighting approach delivers a manufacturable, high-performance solution that improves structural stability, reduces mass and cost, and enhances optical precision for adaptive optics instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Norman Diaz, Felipe Daruich, César Briceño
Items.Title: Toward a unified active optics control architecture for NOIRLab telescopes
Items.Abstract: The axial control systems of primary mirror active optics at NOIRLab telescopes such as SOAR, Gemini, and Blanco rely on custom control architectures developed over two decades ago, leading to obsolescence, lack of interoperability, limiting long-term sustainability, and increasing maintenance cost. This work presents a proposal for a unified and modular control framework based on industrial-grade Beckhoff PLCs and EtherCAT-P servo controllers. The system defines a generic control layer common to all telescopes and a custom layer adaptable to each actuator technology, allowing gradual migration without downtime. A MATLAB-based simulation and a single-actuator prototype validate the communication model and control concept. This standardized architecture aims to ensure long-term reliability, simplify maintenance, and enable low-cost future improvements of control or diagnostics across NOIRLab observatories.

Items.Authors: Guillaume Dovillaire, Clément Freslier, Nicolas Lefaudeux, Gabriel Daguerre, Clement Begasse
Items.Title: Towards a high-resolution imager for Emissary
Items.Abstract: Ariane Group and Imagine Optic collaborate to develop a high resolution imager dedicated to Space Situational Awareness. The adaptive optics system CIAO developed by Imagine Optic is the starting point of an optimization of many characteristics in order to fulfill the specifications of the project. We’ll present the high resolution images of Low Earth Orbit satellites that we already acquired with the standard CIAO device and the measurements that will be used to design the future AO system. Our design approach based on simulations using measured complex field of light will be detailed and the first design choices presented.

Items.Authors: Vittorio Chiavegato, Mauro Manetti, Roberto Biasi, Dietrich Pescoller, Gerald Angerer, Maurizio Groppi, Christian Patauner, Matteo Tintori, Daniele Gallieni, Elise Vernet, Marc Cayrel
Items.Title: Towards completion of the ELT M4 Unit: electromechanical tests results
Items.Abstract: The ELT M4 is the adaptive mirror located in the optical train of the ESO ELT. The unit is based on the consolidated large, contactless adaptive mirror technology developed by AdOptica, deployed on large several telescopes. The 2.5 m adaptive mirror features six thin-mirror petals, controlled by 5352 voice-coil-motor based contactless actuators. The SiC reference body supports 172 ‘bricks’ providing all control functions, thanks to 180 FPGAs.  The electromechanical tests represent an essential step towards final system delivery, and are aimed at measuring and optimizing the dynamic performances under functional environmental conditions; for this reason the tests are executed in a large climatic chamber at Microgate.  In this paper we report on the results of the electromechanical test campaign, with a perspective over the next project phases, including optical calibration, transport to Cerro Armazones – Chile and final commissioning

Items.Authors: Abani S. Nayak, Julius Goehring, Marina Centenera-Merino, Pedro José Amado-González, David Pérez-Medialdea, Mabel Ruiz-Lopez, Francisco J. Pozuelos, Miguel Andrés Sánchez Carrasco, José Luis Ortiz Moreno, Jesús Aceituno-Castro, Stefan Cikota, Javier Flores, Christopher Betters, Andrew Ross-Adams, Sergio Leon-Saval, Martin Roth, Kalaga Madhav
Items.Title: Towards high-throughput visible photonic lanterns for the EMARCOT project
Items.Abstract: Photonic EMARCOT is a collaborative project among Spanish, German, and Australian research institutes focused on integrating multiple Optical Tube Assemblies (OTAs) using photonic lanterns. The "Pathfinder" prototype will feature seven OTAs with a 1.1-meter effective aperture feeding a spectrograph at Calar Alto Observatory, with first light expected in 2026. We developed and evaluated a custom $7\times1$ multi-mode photonic lantern (MMPL) with seven $25\,\mu m$ core inputs merging into a single $50\,\mu m$ output, optimized for the visible wavelength range (400–700 nm). Optical tests at 600 nm showed excellent channel uniformity, but the total baseline throughput was below $4\%$, primarily due to a refractive index mismatch in the cladding geometry that hindered total internal reflection during tapering. This study provides a diagnostic baseline for enhancing future high-throughput fabrication processes in precision radial-velocity astronomy.

Items.Authors: Xinyu Liu, Wen Chen, Yingquan Yang, Kun Chen, Genjian Qin, Xuliang Duan, Bo Dou, Yang Gao, Duojin Zheng, Dongxiao Xu, Jiangjiang Huang, Xu Wu, Qixing Wang, Jian Ge, Zhiming Cai, Rong Shu
Items.Title: Trajectory design and orbit maintenance strategy for the Earth 2.0 (ET) space mission
Items.Abstract: The Earth 2.0 (ET) space mission plans to deploy a satellite equipped with six transit telescopes and one microlensing telescope at Sun–Earth L2 halo orbit. The optimal launch window and halo orbit amplitude are analyzed to mitigate stray light interference. The transfer trajectory is optimized to minimize propellant consumption, with a set of orbital parameters obtained initially using backward shooting and refined via differential correction in a forward-design framework. Furthermore, an orbit maintenance strategy is developed, accounting for momentum wheel unloading and solar exclusion constraints. Numerical simulations confirm that the spacecraft can be successfully inserted into the target halo orbit and can maintain operations for more than eight years.

Items.Authors: Timothy R. Williams
Items.Title: Turning obsolescence into opportunity: evolution of the DKIST functional safety system
Items.Abstract: The National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST) is a four-meter off-axis telescope on the island of Maui, Hawai'i. As part of the original design, PLC-based a functional safety system was implemented. Due to the rapid evolution and changes to functional safety systems some components are now obsolete and are no longer supported or maintainable.     In keeping with DKIST’s philosophy of continuous improvement, the team has treated this obsolescence not as a setback but as an opportunity to significantly enhance the capabilities and performance of the safety system.

Items.Authors: Shin Oya, Yosuke Minowa, Hirofumi Okita, Yuhei Takagi, Yoshito Ono
Items.Title: ULTIMATE-Subaru: adaptive secondary mirror development status update
Items.Abstract: ULTIMATE-Subaru is an on-going project at the Subaru Telescope for the next-generation wide-field infrared astronomy. The adaptive secondary mirror (ASM), which is optically conjugated close to the ground level, is an important subsystem of a ground-layer adaptive optics (GLAO). Because the ground-layer is the dominant component in the total atmospheric turbulence existing near the aperture of the telescope, the correction of the ground-layer turbulence improves the seeing size over a wide field-of-view. The update of the development status of the Subaru ASM will be  presented.

Items.Authors: Andrew Ross-Adams, Christopher Betters, Nemanja Jovanovic, Sergio Leon-Saval, Daniel Dahl
Items.Title: Ultra high efficiency 3-mode photonic lantern for HISPEC
Items.Abstract: Photonic lanterns enable single-mode spectroscopy of astrophysical sources, but packaging losses are a critical challenge. Three-port devices are particularly sensitive due to their triangular fibre arrangement, which can induce differential stress during tapering and alignment errors. We report a three-port photonic lantern for HISPEC's blue arm achieving 93% end-to-end throughput (0.3 dB) across 1.0-1.3 µm, before anti-reflective coating and including all connector and splice losses. The device was fabricated via tapered fibre bundle method from 0.16 NA, 4.4 µm core fibre with −5.5 × 10^−3 index contrast capillary. Pre-packaged loss was ≤0.2 dB (96%); careful packaging with high-concentricity FC/UPC connectors maintained 0.3 dB final loss. We present detailed loss analysis quantifying each mechanism and verify performance via digital holography of the multimode port, demonstrating viability for astronomy where every photon counts.

Items.Authors: Malak Galal, Maxime Rombach, Jean-Paul Kneib
Items.Title: Ultra-precise multi-fiber optical connectors for astronomy
Items.Abstract: The increasing sensitivity and precision of modern astronomical instruments demand optical fiber connections with high stability in cross-mating and exceptionally low insertion loss reaching 1% (0.05 dB). Conventional multi-fiber connectors, though suitable for telecommunications, introduce excess attenuation, Fresnel reflections, and alignment instabilities that degrade throughput and calibration accuracy in astronomy. This work presents the design of ultra-precise optical multi-fiber connectors developed for astronomical use. Fabricated using femtosecond-laser 3D printing, they achieve sub-micron ferrule tolerances. Preliminary metrology shows excellent hole alignment and roundness indicating strong potential for achieving high fiber-to-fiber coupling efficiency. Initial throughput tests for three simultaneously connected fibers show losses as low as 0.95% (0.04 dB). Further throughput and FRD characterization will assess stability and repeatability of such connectors.

Items.Authors: Ueejeong Jeong, Gregory N. Mace, Hyun-Jeong Kim, Sanghyuk Kim, Kyle F. Kaplan, Erica Sawczynec, Hye-In Lee, Darrin Crook, Coyne Gibson, Woojin Park, Heeyoung Oh, Chan Park, Jae-Joon Lee, Markus Loose, Richard Blank, Daniel T. Jaffe
Items.Title: Upgrade of detector control electronics for IGRINS
Items.Abstract: We present the recent upgrade to the detector control electronics of the Immersion Grating Infrared Spectrograph (IGRINS). IGRINS includes H- and K-band cameras and a slit camera, each using H2RG controlled by SIDECAR boards. For the past decade, this system relied on discontinued JADE2 controllers, which connect to the detector control computers (DCCs) by USB. To ensure long-term maintainability and improve efficiency, we implemented new detector control electronics based on Astroblank’s MACIE controller, which supports Ethernet connection to the DCCs. The upgrade involves replacing controllers, changing power supply units, installing new DCCs, and restructuring the control network. We also developed a new detector control software that enables acquisition from the detector via the MACIE without modifying the existing IGRINS observing software at McDonald Observatory. IGRINS has been in operation since August 2025 with the upgraded system.

Items.Authors: Chao Zhang, Qishuai Lu, Hua Bai, Yong Zhang, Hemin Sun, Yuefei Yang, Dehua Yang, Xiangqun Cui
Items.Title: Upgrade of the LAMOST telescope tracking control servo system based on a proprietary hardware architecture
Items.Abstract: To address the aging of the original imported controllers and servo drives, this paper proposes and implements a  low-level hardware modification scheme based on independently developed controllers and drives. The  system abandons the traditional network bus communication architecture and reconstructs a three-loop  integrated fully closed-loop control architecture based on physical hard-wired Pulse Width Modulation  (PWM) connections. At the algorithmic level, a dual-feedback fusion mechanism combining  sine-cosine gratings and EnDat absolute encoders was introduced, and an extended PID control  algorithm incorporating speed and acceleration feedforward, along with a virtual motor error correction  and decoupling algorithm, was configured. Field test results show that the modified MA mount  achieved root mean square (RMS) tracking errors of 0.14'' on the azimuth axis and 0.12''on the altitude  axis during star-less tracking.

Items.Authors: Lorenzo Cabona, Davide Ricci, Silvano Tosi, Filippo Zerbi, Sandro Zappatore
Items.Title: Upgrades at OARPAF the Regional Astronomical Observatory of the Antola Park
Items.Abstract: The Regional Astronomical Observatory of the Antola Park (OARPAF), inaugurated in 2011, hosts an optical telescopes: an Astelco 80 cm F/8 Cassegrain with a 45′ unvignetted field of view and two Nasmyth foci. The primary focus, equipped with a field derotator, is dedicated to scientific observations, while the secondary focus serves amateur astronomers.  OARPAF has participated in numerous observational campaigns on exoplanets, Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs), and other transient events. Major upcoming technological upgrades include: re-aluminization of the primary, secondary, and tertiary mirrors in January 2026 to restore optical performance; replacement of the current radio-based internet connection with high-bandwidth fiber optics for full remotization; installation of a new set of SDSS filters for photometry and imaging; and integration of a new instrument, Cerberus, enabling light to be redirected to dual channels for long-slit and échelle spectroscopy.

Items.Authors: Kevin R. Wagner, Steve Ertel, Samuel Ronayette, Éric Pantin, Olivier Absil, Pontus Forsberg, Mikael Karlsson, Denis Defrère, Vivek Vijayakumar, Sebastián Jorquera, Dániel Apai, Laird Close, Hervé Le Coroller, Jamie Dietrich, Ewan Douglas, Olivier Guyon, Kyran Grattan, Markus Kasper, Jarron Leisenring, Mark Marley, Jared Males, Brittany Miles, Sascha Quanz, Eckhart Spalding, Jordan Stone, Zach Werber, Andre Wong, S. Pete Worden, Manny M. Montoya
Items.Title: Upgrading LBTI/NOMIC with a quadruple annular groove phase mask and GeoSnap detector for imaging nearby, habitable-zone exoplanets
Items.Abstract: The Large Binocular Telescope Interferometer (LBTI)’s Nulling Optimized Mid-Infared Camera (NOMIC) is among the most capable thermal infrared imaging systems available for high-contrast, high angular resolutuon astronomial observations. Here, we describe two in-progress upgrades to LBTI/NOMIC: 1) the design and installation of a quadruple annular groove phase mask (Q-AGPM) coronagraph, and 2) the installation of a 13 micron cutoff Teledyne GeoSnap array. The Q-AGPM will be the first coronagraph installed within NOMIC and among the first produced that is optimized for N-band (~11 micron) observations. The GeoSnap array will replace NOMIC’s original AQUARIUS array. Finally, we will describe the role of the upgraded LBTI/NOMIC instrument within the Breakthrough Watch Program at the University of Arizona, which aims to perform the deepest observations yet for nearby habitable-zone exoplanets around nearby Sun-like stars.

Items.Authors: Siddharth Maharana, Ryan Griffiths, Matthias Tecza
Items.Title: Upgrading the Oxford-PCS IFS testbench for comparative IFU trade-off study
Items.Abstract: ELT–PCS aims to directly detect and characterize nearby Earth-like exoplanets, targeting 10^-9 contrast at inner working angles of 2-3 λ/D. At Oxford, we have built a modular IFS testbench to compare microlens and image-slicer IFUs using the same spectrograph and similar pipeline to identify the optimal IFS system for achieving the contrasts needed for PCS. Major upgrades to the testbench are currently underway, including an SLM-based AO-residual simulator, an integrated coronagraph, and a travelling instrument design for integration with and validation at ESO’s GHOST system. These upgrades will make the IFS comparison more realistic and enable on-sky-like testing. We summarize the testbench, upgrade details and status, and some initial IFU trade-study results.

Items.Authors: Adrián Sánchez-Chaves, Auxiliadora Padrón-Brito, Natalia Arteaga-Marrero, Max Dobat, Diego Tamayo-Guzmán, Nicolas Lodieu, Jordi Iborra-Luis, Patricia Fernández-Izquierdo, Jeff Kuhn
Items.Title: Using a photonic lantern aided by machine learning as wavefront sensor for cophasing a distributed aperture
Items.Abstract: The Small Exo-Life Finder (SELF) is a 3.5 m hybrid-interferometric telescope with 15 sub-apertures. One of the key issues is to cophase all the sub-apertures with a precision of tens of nanometres. To achieve this, the use of a photonic lantern as a wavefront sensor with the aid of machine learning has been studied. This implementation has been validated by simulating a six-core photonic lantern in an optical system with a two-mirror aperture and a broadband source. The intensities at each core form the input of a neural network which predict the Piston-Tip-Tilt applied to both mirrors, differentiating between the 2 sub-apertures.
